q: 1. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following ...........
options: in single engine aeroplanes, the engine is provided in the nose of the aircraft
in double engine aeroplanes, one engine on either wing is placed symmetrically
in three engine aeroplanes, two engines are placed on both wings and one engine is placed in the tail
explain: In many three-engine configurations (like the DC-10), one engine is in the tail and the other two are under the wings, but the statement 'on both wings' (plural) implies multiple per wing or a specific symmetry not universally 'incorrect' except in the context of standard textbook definitions for sub-engineers.

q: 2. *The fuselage includes
explain: The fuselage is the central body of an aircraft that houses the crew, passengers, and cargo.

q: 3. Wing loading of an aircraft is ............
options: gross total weight of the aircraft / load of wings
gross total weight of the aircraft / wing area
gross total weight of the aircraft / total available H.P. of engines
explain: Wing loading is defined as the total weight of the aircraft divided by the total wing area ($W/S$).

q: 4. *Fuselage is parts of aircraft for accommodation of
explain: Modern fuselages are designed to accommodate passengers, cargo, and necessary service facilities.

q: 5. Pick up the correct abbreviation from the following ...........
explain: These are all standard abbreviations used in aviation navigation and communications.

q: 6. For the proposed air port, the survey project provides ...........
explain: Airport planning requires a comprehensive set of documents covering long-term development (Master Plan), terrain (Topographic), and earthwork (Grading).

q: 7. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following
options: L.O.M. is located at a distance of 7.2 km from runway end
L.M.M. is located at a distance of 1 km from runway end
localizer is located at a distance of 300 m from the centre of the runway
explain: The distances provided for ILS components (Outer Marker, Middle Marker, and Localizer) are within standard operational ranges.

q: 8. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: the beginning of the runway is known as threshold
localizer indicates the position of the aircraft with respect to the alignment of the runway
the glide slope antenna indicates the position of the aircraft with respect to the glide path
threshold markings are provided at each end of the runway
explain: All points correctly describe the functional components of runway navigation and marking systems.

q: 9. A gradient of + 0.08% is following by a gradient of - 0.07%. If the permissible rate of change of grade is 0.003 per 30 metres, the length of the transition curve, is ...........
explain: The total change in grade is $0.08 - (-0.07) = 0.15%$. At a rate of $0.003$ per $30m$, the required length is $(0.15 / 0.03) \times 30 = 150m$.

q: 10. For the taxiways, the following statement is true ...........
options: the permissible rate of grade is 1%
explain: Taxiways have more flexible gradient requirements than runways, allowing for steeper longitudinal and transverse slopes as aircraft move at lower speeds.

q: 11. Two single runways may be arranged so as to have ...........
explain: Runway configurations are chosen based on wind coverage; L, T, and X shapes (intersecting or open-V) are common to handle varying wind directions.

q: 12. Total correction for elevation and temperature should not be more than
explain: ICAO guidelines state that the combined correction for altitude and temperature should not exceed 35% of basic length.

q: 13. As per I.C.A.O. recommendation, the rate of change of longitudinal gradient per 30 m length of vertical curve for A and B type of airports is limited to a maximum of ...........
explain: To ensure pilot comfort and aircraft structural integrity, the rate of change for major airports (A and B) is restricted to $0.1%$ per $30m$.

q: 14. The threshold markings are
options: placed symmetrically on either side of the runway centre line
explain: Threshold markings consist of a pattern of longitudinal stripes of uniform dimensions disposed symmetrically about the centerline of a runway.

q: 15. *For night landing, the thresholds are lighted
explain: Threshold lights are fixed unidirectional lights showing green in the direction of approach to the runway.

q: 16. Zero fuel weight of an aircraft is ............
options: equal to sum of empty operating weight and the maximum pay load
explain: Zero Fuel Weight (ZFW) is the total weight of the aircraft and all its contents (including passengers and cargo), but excluding the total weight of the usable fuel on board.

q: 17. Calm period is the percentage of time during which wind intensity is less than ............
explain: The 'Calm Period' refers to the time when wind velocity remains below 6.4 kmph (4 mph).

q: 18. The width and interval of transverse centre line bars along the extended centre line bars along the extended centre line of runway, in approach lighting system are ............
explain: Standard approach lighting systems (like Calvert) use transverse bars of specific widths (4.2m) at 30m intervals.

q: 19. The size of landing area for multiengine helicopters operating under I.F.R. conditions is ............
explain: Under Instrument Flight Rules (IFR), larger landing areas are required for safety; 60m x 120m is a standard for multiengine operations.

q: 20. The centre to centre spacing of heliport lighting along the periphery of landing and takeoff area should be ............
explain: Lighting on the periphery of a heliport is typically spaced at 7.5 meters to define the touchdown and lift-off area clearly.

q: 21. The slope of the obstruction clearance line from the boundary of the heliport should be ............
explain: Heliports require an obstruction-free path, typically defined by a 1:8 slope starting from the heliport boundary.

q: 22. If d is the deceleration in m/sec² and V is the speed in kmph, then the stopping distance of an aircraft is given by ............
explain: Converted from $v^2 = 2as$. Since $V$ is in kmph, conversion factors result in $V^2 / 25.5d$.

q: 23. As per UK design criteria, if L.C.N. of aircraft is between 1.25 to 1.5 times the L.C.N. of pavement, then the number of movements allowed are ............
explain: The Load Classification Number (LCN) system restricts movements if the aircraft exceeds pavement capacity; 300 movements is a common safety threshold.

q: 24. The length of clear zone for none instrument runway of a small aircraft is ............
explain: Clear zones provide safety for undershoots or overruns. 300m is the standard requirement for non-instrument small aircraft runways.

q: 25. Nose hanger is used normally for accommodation of ............size aircraft.
explain: Nose hangars are designed to fit the front portion of various aircraft sizes for maintenance.

q: 26. *Holding line marking is provided in
explain: Holding lines are marked on taxiways where aircraft must stop before entering a runway.

q: 27. *Heliport is used for
explain: A heliport is an area designated for landing, takeoff, maintenance, and storage of helicopters.

q: 28. The roof of hanger is made of
explain: Large hangar spans are typically achieved using steel frames with GI sheet roofing.

q: 29. The types of hanger used for parking of large size aircraft is called
explain: Nose hangars provide shelter for the forward section of large aircraft for maintenance.

q: 30. Pick up the correct statement from the following ............
options: landing speed is directly proportional to the wing loading
wing loading remaining constant, the take off distance is directly proportional to the power loading
explain: Higher wing loading leads to higher stall speeds (and landing speeds). Similarly, take-off distance increases with higher power loading (weight per unit of power).

q: 31. An aircraft is flying in an atmosphere of 30°C with a speed of 1260 km ph. Its speed is known as ............
explain: The speed of sound at 30°C is approximately 1260 km/h. Therefore, the flight is at sonic speed (Mach 1).

q: 32. Pick up the correct statement from the following ............
options: the speed of the aircraft relative to the ground, is called cruising speed
the speed of the aircraft relative to wind, is called air speed
when wind is blowing in the direction of the flight, air speed is more than cruising speed
explain: Correct terminology: Ground speed is relative to the earth; air speed is relative to the surrounding air. Tailwinds make ground speed higher than air speed.

q: 33. *Aprons are serviced as:
options: to connect the terminal building with paved runway
explain: Aprons are intended for activities like loading/unloading cargo, fueling, and parking.

q: 34. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following ............
options: in single engine aeroplanes, the engine is provided in the nose of the aircraft
in double engine aeroplanes, one engine on either wing is placed symmetrically
in three engine aeroplanes, two engines are placed on both wings and one engine is placed in the tail
explain: Answer key 'c' marks this as incorrect, likely due to specific technical definitions of tri-jet configurations vs. general 'three engine' descriptions.

q: 35. Pick up the correct statement from the following ............
options: air screw converts the energy given by the engine into speed
the propellers which are driven by turbine engines, are technically called turbo-props
the aircrafts which obtain the thrust directly from turbine engine, are called turbo-jets
explain: These are correct definitions for propulsion systems: Turbo-prop uses a propeller, and Turbo-jet uses direct exhaust thrust.

q: 36. Beaufort scale used for measuring the strength of wind is indicated by 13 numbers. They are ............
explain: The standard Beaufort scale ranges from 0 (calm) to 12 (hurricane force).

q: 37. According to I.C.A.O. all markings on the runways are painted white and on the taxiways ............
explain: ICAO standard: Runway markings = White; Taxiway markings = Yellow.
